Addr.description: an address and port such as 192.0.2.1:443 or [2001:db8::1]:443

proxy_only.description: Defaults to true on a socks5 outbound. Must be absent or false on a direct one.

oneOf.description: The entry half of node links: what is routed to the exit leaves from another node, through one of these links.

links.description: The tags of 1 to 4 links that lead to the same exit node. Each is a link whose entry half this node is.

Certificate.description: The certificate of a native `tls` transport: files the operator obtains with their own tooling, or one the node makes itself.

Decoy.description: The decoy origin of a stream listener: the operator's own web server, which answers everyone who is not a user.

proxy_protocol.description: Whether the node sends the PROXY protocol header, version 2, at the start of every connection to the origin. Defaults to false.

preshared_key.description: A secret. No diagnostic, log line or `Debug` output shows it.

transport_secrets.description: One, or two while the secret is rotated. Needed by a device with an address in a `veilway` inbound.

sets.description: Other lists of servers, each for the inbounds, groups and users it names. Whoever no set names asks `servers`.

DnsSet.description: A set that names a user decides for that user, before one that names a group of theirs, before one that names the inbound a query came through.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to the tag.

GatewayNet.description: a gateway address with its prefix such as 10.7.0.1/24

Host.description: an IP address or a lowercase host name, with no port

HostPort.description: a host and port such as proxy.example.com:1080, with an IPv6 address in brackets

Http2.description: `http2` of a `tls` transport: whether the node offers HTTP/2 next to HTTP/1.1 once it ends TLS. Off by default, because the node's own HTTP/2 server answers a prober where the decoy origin's would otherwise.

mtu.description: Defaults to 1420, and to 1390 for a `veilway` inbound with a `udp-obfs` transport.

padding.description: The upper bounds of the padding the node puts on what it sends over the obfuscated transports of a `veilway` inbound.

private_key.description: A secret. No diagnostic, log line or `Debug` output shows it.

transport_keys.description: The node transport keys, private halves: one, or two while the key is rotated. Needed by an inbound with a `tls`, native `ws` or `fronted` transport. Profiles carry the public half of the first.

upgrade_cookie.description: The name of the cookie on the upgrade answer of a `tls` or native `ws` transport. It has no default and carries no meaning: its value is random text of a random length.

upgrade_headers.description: The header fields the upgrade answer takes from the decoy origin, in this order. Defaults to `Server`, `Date` for a `tls` transport and to none for a native `ws` transport, where the web server in front adds its own.

oneOf.description: Plain WireGuard. Its gateway answers DNS and ping, and nothing else.
The same tunnel with the control channel at its gateway address. Every device with an address in it has a transport secret.

Ip.description: an IPv4 or IPv6 address without a prefix

IpEntry.description: a network such as 10.7.0.0/24 with no host bits set, geoip:private, tunnel:users or tunnel:<inbound tag>

Key.description: a WireGuard key: 44 characters of standard base64 with padding

Link.description:
One node link, as its pairing left it on this node. A link with `inbound` and `public_key` is one this node is dialled for, and a link with `peer` and `private_key` one it dials.
With `direction`, that says which half the node is: the exit half when it is dialled in a forward link or dials a reverse one, and the entry half otherwise. The entry half is used through an exit with a `chain` backend.

allow_private.description: On the exit half: whether private networks are decided by the rules for this link. Defaults to false, which refuses them whatever the rules say.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. A link that is not enabled is validated like any other and neither dialled nor answered.

exit.description: On the exit half: the exit the link leaves through when no rule names one. Without it that is `routing.default`.

exits.description: On the exit half, where it is needed: the exits the link may leave through. None of them is a `chain` exit.

inbound.description: On the node that is dialled: the tag of the `veilway` inbound the link connects to. That inbound carries no users' devices.

max_flows.description: On the exit half: the flows the link may have at once. Defaults to 16384.

mtu.description: Defaults to 1390 when the link lists `udp-obfs`, and to 1420 otherwise.

peer.description: On the node that dials: the other node's keys and transports.

private_key.description: A secret. No diagnostic, log line or `Debug` output shows it.

public_key.description: On the node that is dialled: the WireGuard public key the other node made for this link.

quota_bytes.description: On the exit half. The quota and its period mean what they mean for a user.

transport_secret.description: The secret the two nodes agreed on when they were paired. It never travels.

LinkAddresses.description: The addresses pairing fixed for a link, all from the inbound pool of the node the link connects to.

dialler.description: The address of the node that dials: at most one IPv4 and one IPv6.

listener.description: The link address of the node that is dialled, in a reverse link and in no other: one for each family of `dialler`.

LinkCandidate.description: One way to reach the other node of a link through its web server or directly, as a profile of a subscription writes a candidate.

pins.description: Needed by a `tls` candidate. The certificate chain is always validated, and a pin is a second condition.

sni.description: The server name that is shown, or empty for none.

verify_name.description: The name the certificate is held against when `sni` is empty, and only then.

LinkDirection.description: Who dials. In a forward link the entry dials the exit, in a reverse link the exit dials the entry.

LinkId.description: the id of a link: 22 characters of base64url without padding

LinkPeer.description: What the node that dials a link holds of the node it dials, "as the offer gave them".

inbound_public_key.description: The WireGuard public key of the inbound the link connects to.

transport_public_key.description: The node transport public key of that inbound. Needed when a `tls` or `ws` transport is listed.

transports.description: In the other node's order of preference.

LinkTransport.description: One transport of the node a link dials, in the shape a profile of a subscription has: `endpoints` for `udp` and `udp-obfs`, `path` and `candidates` for `tls` and `ws`.

oneOf.description: Read so that validation can say why a link has none.

destinations.description: Whether log lines may contain the destinations and DNS names users reach.

Origin.description: an http:// URL of the operator's own web server with nothing behind the host and port, such as http://127.0.0.1:8080. This build has no https:// origin

password.description: A secret. No diagnostic, log line or `Debug` output shows it.

username.description: A secret. No diagnostic, log line or `Debug` output shows it.

Padding.description: Transports page, "Padding", rule 4: the bounds "may be set per profile for the client and per inbound for the node, inside the bounds in the table of numbers".

normal.description: The most bytes of normal padding. Defaults to 255.

wide.description: The most bytes of wide padding. Defaults to 1023.

Pin.description: a certificate pin: 44 characters of standard base64 with padding

ProofRate.description: Accepted proofs one source may bring: `burst` at once, then `rate` a second. A source is an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64.

Proxy.description: an address such as 127.0.0.1 or a network such as 10.0.0.0/8 with no host bits set

cache.description: How many accepted proofs the node remembers at once. Defaults to 262144. It is read at start: a reload that changes it changes nothing until the node starts again.

per_source.description: Defaults to a burst of 256 and 32 a second.

Rule.description: Every condition that is present must hold. A condition that is present is never an empty list.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. Not a condition: a disabled rule is validated like any other and skipped when flows are matched.

link.description: The tags of node links whose exit half this node is: the rule matches what arrives from one of them. A link has no user and no group.

SelfSigned.description: `{"self_signed": true}`: the node makes an ECDSA P-256 key and a self-signed certificate on its first start, keeps them next to the config file with mode 600, makes the certificate anew with the same key before it runs out, and reports the pin, the SHA-256 of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo, that profiles carry with `self_signed`.

name.description: The operator's own host name, which the certificate carries as its subject and its alternative name. Without it the node draws a name per node and keeps it.

Shape.description: The shape of a `fronted-shaped` transport, as the profile of its subscription carries it. The members are those of the shapes page, and the panel writes one object to the config and to the profile.

ShapeDown.description: The downstream half of a shape.

fallback.description: Whether the client may fall back to polling when streams do not work. Only with `sse`. Defaults to true.

gather.description: Milliseconds the node waits to collect datagrams into one event, `[low, high]`, 0 to 250 each. Only with `sse`. Defaults to `[0, 20]`.

life.description: The range in seconds a stream's length is drawn from, `[low, high]`, 30 to 3600 each. Only with `sse`. Defaults to `[120, 900]`.

mode.description: `poll`: answers carry the downstream data. `sse`: one Server-Sent Events stream does.

ShapeUp.description: The upstream half of a shape. Which methods go with which `in`, and the bounds of every number, are validation's.

gather.description: Milliseconds the client waits to collect datagrams into one request, drawn from `[low, high]`, 0 to 250 each. Defaults to `[10, 60]`.

in.description: Where the data of a request goes. `GET` takes `query`, `path` or `header`; `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH` take `body`; a custom method takes any.

inflight.description: Requests that may be in flight at once, not counting the stream. 1 to 4. Defaults to 1 with `poll` and 2 with `sse`, and is 1 with `poll`.

limit.description: The most one request carries, as bytes of body, of request target or of header value. 1024 to 8000 for `query` and `path` (default 4000), 1024 to 4096 for `header` (default 3000), 1024 to 65536 for `body` (default 65536).

method.description: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or a custom method of 3 to 16 capital letters. `CONNECT`, `TRACE`, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` are refused.

name.description: The name of the one header field that carries the data. Required with `header` and refused otherwise.

Site.description: The real site a `faketls` transport borrows (borrowed-site page, "Config and profile fields"). The site is a third party that has not agreed to anything: the operator chooses it, and `acknowledged` says the operator knows what that means.

acknowledged.description: Must be true. Every stranger's connection and every early connection of a user is a connection to a site whose owner has not agreed, from this node's address, and using its name may break its terms of use or the law where the operator is.

address.description: An address and port to connect to instead of resolving `host`.

host.description: The site's name: the only server name a user's hello may carry besides `names`, and the name of the connections the node relays to the site.

names.description: Extra server names that a user's hello may carry. At most 4.

Source.description: an address such as 192.0.2.1 or a network such as 192.0.2.0/24 with no host bits set

Timestamp.description: an RFC 3339 timestamp with an offset such as 2027-01-31T00:00:00Z

oneOf.description: WireGuard datagrams inside the `udp-obfs` envelope, for a `veilway` inbound.
The native WebSocket session inside TLS that the node ends itself, for a `veilway` inbound. Whoever is not a user is relayed to `decoy.origin`.

http2.description: `on`: the node offers `h2` and `http/1.1`, decides every stream on its own and relays a stranger's streams to the decoy origin as HTTP/1.1. `off` (the default): `http/1.1` alone.

path.description: The path a proof arrives on, which the origin must serve nothing at.

oneOf.description: The borrowed-site transport of a `veilway` inbound (alpha, new and unreviewed): the node holds no certificate, a client proves itself inside its first TLS message, and every other connection is relayed to the real `site`. `limits` takes `relayed` and `site_rate` alone.

transport_key.description: The private half of the transport's own key: no other transport of the node may have it.

oneOf.description: The native WebSocket session behind the operator's own web server, for a `veilway` inbound: `ws` with a `decoy`. The node never ends TLS here. It reads plain HTTP from `trusted_proxies`, and whoever is not a user is answered by `decoy.origin`.

client_address_header.description: The header field in which the proxies name the address a request came from, such as `X-Forwarded-For`. Without it every visitor counts as the proxy itself.

path.description: The path a proof arrives on, as the web server in front hands it on, which the origin must serve nothing at.

trusted_proxies.description: The operator's own reverse proxies, as addresses and networks. Only a connection from one of them can carry a user, and only from them is `client_address_header` believed.

oneOf.description: Polling with HTTP requests through a CDN that allows nothing better, behind the operator's own web server, for a `veilway` inbound. Its keys are those of the native `ws`.

`fronted` whose requests and answers are in the shape this transport names (protocol, "Shapes of fronted"): which method carries the data, where in the request it goes, and whether the node answers each request or writes to one event stream. Its keys are those of `fronted`, and its proofs are valid on no other transport.

TransportKey.description: a transport key: 44 characters of standard base64 with padding

TransportLimits.description: Node capacity numbers of one listener (transports page, "Numbers that are judgement calls").

decoy_requests_per_source.description: Requests one source may have waiting for the decoy origin at once on a `ws` or `fronted` listener. Defaults to 16.

fronted_sessions.description: Established `fronted` sessions the listener holds at once, each of which keeps its last response, up to 65536 bytes. Defaults to 1024, which is 64 MiB when full.

proxy_connections.description: Connections from `trusted_proxies` a `ws` or `fronted` listener holds at once. Defaults to twice its `fronted_sessions`. Requests of strangers that wait for the decoy origin hold at most half of them.

relayed.description: Connections of a stream listener that are relayed to the decoy origin. Defaults to 1024.

sessions.description: Established sessions the listener holds at once. Defaults to 16384.

shaped_sessions.description: Established `fronted-shaped` sessions the listener holds at once, counted among its `fronted_sessions`. Each can hold up to 603136 bytes. Defaults to 256, which is about 147 MiB when full.

site_rate.description: New connections a second that a `faketls` listener opens to its site, for the relay of strangers and the early connections together. Only on `faketls`. Defaults to 16. When it is spent, users are still served.

undecided.description: Connections of a stream listener that have not sent their request line yet. Defaults to 512.

undecided_per_source.description: How many of those one source may have. A source is an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64. Defaults to 64.

TransportSecret.description: a transport secret: 44 characters of standard base64 with padding

Tunnel.description: A tunnel (node links page, "Tunnels"): one TCP or UDP port of this node forwarded to one address on the far side of a node link, through a `chain` exit, with no client.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. A tunnel that is not enabled is validated and does not listen.

listen.description: The address this node listens on. No other tunnel, inbound transport or listener of this node uses the same address, port and protocol.

max_connections.description: TCP connections or UDP sessions at once. Defaults to 256. One client address holds at most 16.

sources.description: The networks that may connect. Without it, a tunnel that listens on an address that is not loopback is a warning.

target.description: The address the far node is asked to reach. Not a link address, not inside an inbound pool of this node, and nothing the destination gate refuses. A private address works only when the far node set `allow_private` for the link.

other.description: Defaults to "reject". "local" and "direct" are not allowed.

Xray.description: The Xray add-on's part of the config. Xray runs as a child of the node and only ever reaches the network through the node: its traffic is attributed to the user of the client, and the node's gate, rules, exits and quotas apply to it.

secret.description: A UUID for `vless`. For `trojan` a password of 22 to 128 characters from A-Z a-z 0-9 and _ - . + / =. For `shadowsocks` a key of 32 bytes as standard base64. No two clients of an inbound share a secret.

clients.description: The users that may use this inbound, each with the credential they present to it.

decoy.description: Where a connection that is not a user's goes after the TLS handshake: the operator's own web server, the same one the `decoy.origin` of a `tls` transport names. Required for `vless` and `trojan`, not allowed for `shadowsocks`.

server_key.description: The server's key for `shadowsocks`: 32 bytes as standard base64. Required for `shadowsocks`, not allowed for the others.

tls.description: The certificate files of the listener. Required for `vless` and `trojan`, and not allowed for `shadowsocks`, which encrypts itself.

oneOf.description: Needs `tls` and a `decoy`. The client secret is a UUID.
Needs `tls` and a `decoy`. The client secret is a password.
The cipher is 2022-blake3-aes-256-gcm with a key for the server and one per client. Every key is 32 bytes as standard base64.

links.description: The node links of this node: each joins it to one other node, so that users connect to one of the two and their traffic leaves from the other.

notices.description: What the operator tells every device on the control channel of a `veilway` inbound, as plain text.

public_addresses.description: The addresses a profile of this node is given, as host names or IP addresses with no port: each transport keeps the port of its own listener.

replay.description: The replay memory of the obfuscated transports. Only a node with such a transport keeps one.

tunnels.description: The ports of this node that are forwarded through a `chain` exit to an address on the far side of a node link, with no client.

xray.description: The Xray add-on: inbounds of Xray that carry the users listed in their `clients`. Off when the key is absent.
